# A dock tab hidden by the header overflow gets no "More tabs" control

## Context

Found during the 13.3 release testing on `dev` `7835b3d332`, with headless branded Chrome at 1400×900 on `examples/dashboard/dock`. The dock projects `Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow` into each group's header action rail (`projectAsAction: true`, `src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs`). When the tabs no longer fit, the plugin collapses the overflowing ones behind a "More tabs" control whose menu reaches them.

## The Problem

After one particular sequence, the plugin hides a tab but renders no control, so that pane can no longer be reached:

1. Load `examples/dashboard/dock`. The first group holds Strategy…History, 675 px wide, and its rail shows only `close`.
2. Drag the splitter between the first group and Terminal 180 px to the left, which leaves the group 495 px wide. All seven tabs still fit (the last ends at 437 px) and the rail still shows only `close`.
3. Drag the History tab to the front of the same strip.

Observed, still the same 2.5 s and 3.8 s after the drop:
- The rail now shows four actions: `lock@415`, `reload@435`, `maximize@455` and `close@475`.
- The strip shows History, Strategy, Swarm, Metrics, Timeline, Agents. Alerts' header is not in the DOM; its pane is still there, collapsed to 0 px.
- No `.neo-tab-overflow-control` exists anywhere in the document. Nothing on screen reaches Alerts.

The same reorder at full width keeps all seven tabs. Dragging Alerts to the front instead drops History in the same way. A plain click on History in the narrowed group leaves the rail at `close` and hides nothing. No console or page errors occur.

## The Architectural Reality

- Hiding Alerts is the plugin's correct answer for a 4-action rail: 438 px of tabs exceed the room before `lock@415`. The defect is the missing control. The plugin's contract (`src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs`, class summary) is that overflowing tabs collapse behind one control whose menu reaches them, and in action mode that control is a toolbar action the plugin keeps hidden only while everything fits.
- The rail grows to four actions only after the drop; the click alone does not do it. So the trigger is the projection the reorder runs, which lands a new rail and a new hidden set together. Whether the control is dropped by the consumer's `actions` replacement or never contributed for this pass is open.
- The action-mode overflow shipped in 13.2.0 (`#17960`, 2026-08-31). This sequence was not run on 13.2.0, so whether it is a regression is unverified.

## The Fix

Find which side loses the control in this projection (the plugin's action contribution, or the toolbar's preservation of it across the `actions` replacement), and keep it whenever the hidden set is non-empty. Witness the sequence above in a browser e2e beside the existing tab-overflow coverage: red at base, green at head.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 After the sequence above, the first group shows a "More tabs" control whose menu lists Alerts, and picking it activates Alerts.
- [ ] AC-2 A browser e2e reproduces the sequence; it fails on the current `dev` and passes with the fix.
- [ ] AC-3 With everything fitting (full width), the control stays hidden, as today.

## Out of Scope

- Why the reorder grows the rail to four actions; that may be intended (the dropped group becomes active), and the control must hold either way.
- The multi-window dock battery.

- 2026-10-20T12:05:21Z @tobiu referenced in commit `f639be4` - "fix(dock): a reordered group keeps its tab-overflow control (#19885) (#19895)

Reconciler.moveRetainedTabChrome switched the tab bar's overflow control
to hideMode 'visibility' on every retained-chrome move. That transport
hold was written for the floating control. Since #17960 the dock's
control is a toolbar action, hidden by removeDom while every tab fits.
Once a reorder had switched its mode, show() only cleared the visibility
style, the removed node never returned, and the group's hidden tabs could
not be reached. The hold now applies only to a floating control, matching
the restore that already skips action mode.

The new e2e case swaps two tabs at full width, then narrows the viewport
until the group overflows. It is red without the fix, because the control
never appears, and green with it."
